dimensions.assessment: Federal financial institutions regulatory agencies, insured depository institutions, and credit unions.
dimensions.evidence: Each Federal financial institutions regulatory agency shall conduct an internal review of the cumulative impact of regulations

dimensions.assessment: Imposes recurring administrative and analytical duties on regulators to evaluate the cumulative costs, benefits, and market liquidity impacts of regulations.
dimensions.evidence: The bill increases this frequency to every 7 years. Additionally, the bill expands these reviews to include an internal review of the cumulative impacts of regulations

dimensions.assessment: Involves internal agency administrative reviews with no direct federal budget outlays or tax changes.
dimensions.evidence: Each Federal financial institutions regulatory agency shall conduct an internal review of the cumulative impact of regulations

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Economic Growth and Regulatory Paperwork Reduction Act of 1996 to alter agency review timelines and add statutory evaluation requirements.
dimensions.evidence: Section 2222 of the Economic Growth and Regulatory Paperwork Reduction Act of 1996 (12 U.S.C. 3311) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent statutory cycle requiring reviews every 7 years.
dimensions.evidence: by striking 'once every 10 years' and inserting 'once every 7 years'

missing_information: Administrative costs for federal financial agencies to carry out the expanded reviews are not quantified.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill increases the frequency of regulatory reviews by financial agencies from every 10 years to every 7 years and expands them to include cumulative impact assessments.
